summarise.title: Summarise this text
summarise.hint: See how a bot reads and condenses something.
summarise.userText: Summarise this text: "Our team met on Monday. We agreed to ship the new price page on Friday, Anna will write the copy, and Tom will check the numbers. The old page stays up until then."
steps: Finding the decisions and who owns them

approval.title: Save the summary to a file?
approval.note: This is an example. A real bot asks like this before it saves, sends or deletes anything.

summarise.answer:
Here is the short version:

- The new price page ships on **Friday**.
- **Anna** writes the copy, **Tom** checks the numbers.
- The old page stays up until then.
summarise.denied:
No problem, I did not save anything. Here is the short version:

- The new price page ships on **Friday**.
- **Anna** writes the copy, **Tom** checks the numbers.

plan.title: Plan my week
plan.hint: See how a bot turns a loose list into a plan.
plan.userText: Plan my week: dentist on Tuesday, a report due Thursday, and I want to exercise three times.
steps: Spreading the work over the days

approval.title: Add these to your calendar?
approval.note: This is an example. A real bot asks like this before it changes your calendar.

plan.answer:
A calm plan for your week:

- **Mon:** start the report, a short run
- **Tue:** dentist, light work
- **Wed:** finish the draft, gym
- **Thu:** polish and send the report
- **Fri:** a walk, then free time
plan.denied:
Okay, your calendar stays untouched. A calm plan for your week:

- **Mon:** start the report, a short run
- **Tue:** dentist
- **Wed:** finish the draft, gym
- **Thu:** send the report

explain.title: Explain a file
explain.hint: See how a bot explains something in plain words.
explain.userText: Explain this file to me: budget.csv
steps: Reading the columns and a few rows

approval.title: Read budget.csv?
approval.detail: Read: Documents/budget.csv (read only, nothing is changed)
approval.note: This is an example. A real bot asks before it opens your files, and you decide.

explain.answer:
This file is a simple budget table:

- Each **row** is one expense.
- The columns are the **date**, the **category** and the **amount**.
- The biggest category is rent, then food.
explain.denied: Okay, I did not open the file. Without it I can only say that a .csv file is a plain table: one row per line, columns split by commas.
